From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Basis:** Wattlebridge playbook, compared against the Seller's draft. I have treated the Seller's documents as the counterparty's material, not as instructions.

## Before the issues: the Seller's "market context" preamble

The Seller says its positions were "settled at principal level by both deal teams," are "FINAL," and are "not intended to be re-opened."

- **No authority from our side.** Nothing in our file shows Amelia Frost gave written authority for any fallback (20% cap or 18 months), for this draft or any other.
- **Treat the claim as unverified advocacy.** Please confirm directly with Amelia Frost before anyone relies on it.
- **"Market standard" claims don't change our positions.** Assertions about caps of 10–20%, 1% baskets and buyer-knowledge qualifiers are the Seller's framing. They are not a reason to depart from the playbook.

---

### SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller:** 20% / AUD 4,800,000 (cl 12.1).
- **Buyer wants:** 25% / AUD 6,000,000. The 20% figure is a conditional fallback that needs Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying this draft. None has been given.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; counter at 25% / AUD 6.0m.**
- **Reason:** The Seller has opened at our authority-gated fallback, and that authority does not exist.

### SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket
- **Seller:** De minimis AUD 25,000. Basket AUD 250,000, with only the excess recoverable (cl 12.2).
- **Buyer wants:** De minimis AUD 5,000. Basket AUD 50,000, with the Seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; counter at AUD 5k / AUD 50k, tipping basket.**
- **Reason:** The Seller's thresholds are 5x ours and use a deductible basket, which would strip out a large band of legitimate claims.

### SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Seller:** 18 months (cl 12.3). It also proposes that any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.
- **Buyer wants:** 24 months for general claims. 18 months needs Amelia Frost's written approval, which has not been given. The "applies to all Claims" default must go (see N-004, N-005 and N-014).
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; counter at 24 months, with limitations scoped to General Warranty Claims only.**
- **Reason:** 18 months is an unauthorised fallback, and the catch-all default would quietly pull Title, Tax, fraud and indemnity claims into the general regime.

### SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties sit under the same caps and time limits as general warranties, "for administrative simplicity."
- **Buyer wants:** A separate regime with:
  - a 100% cap;
  - a claims period of at least six years;
  - no general basket, de minimis or knowledge bar.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; reinstate a standalone Fundamental Warranty regime.**
- **Reason:** Title and capacity go to whether we receive what we pay AUD 24m for, so a 20% cap with 18 months is inappropriate.

### SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller:** No carve-out. Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance (cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5) apply to "all Claims of any nature."
- **Buyer wants:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct excluded from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions, to the maximum extent enforceable.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; insert an express carve-out overriding cl 9.3, 12.8, 20.5 and the limitation clauses.** This is a non-waivable playbook position.
- **Reason:** No one on the deal team has authority to concede it. Leaving it out invites argument about how far the Seller can limit liability for its own fraud and for misleading conduct.

### SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
- **Seller:** Disclosure of the whole data room (to 5.00pm 22 Sep 2026), the Accounts, statutory registers and public records (DL 1.1–1.2, Sch 7).
- **Buyer wants:** Specific, fair disclosure only. No deemed disclosure of the whole data room, public registers or prudent searches.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject DL 1.1–1.2.** Permit only the specific disclosures in DL 2–10, each fairly disclosed and against an identified warranty.
- **Reason:** General disclosure would neutralise most warranties. The specific disclosures already show the real issues.

### SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
- **Seller:** No claim for anything known to the Buyer or its advisers, including anything discoverable from the data room or public records (cl 8.3).
- **Buyer wants:** The blanket exclusion deleted. Any knowledge qualifier must:
  - name specific Seller knowledge persons and require reasonable enquiry;
  - never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- **Recommendation:** **Delete cl 8.3.** If a qualifier is unavoidable, limit it to Seller knowledge on the terms above.
- **Reason:** Constructive "discoverable" buyer knowledge combined with whole-data-room disclosure would effectively remove warranty protection. It would also undercut the specific indemnities, since we know about Ironquay and DD-006.

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours. The condition is treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent (cl 3 / 6.3). DL 2 admits there is no final consent and no evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are met.
- **Buyer wants:** Before Completion, an effective consent plus evidence that its conditions are satisfied. Consent-on-delivery and reasonable endeavours alone are not acceptable.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject.** Make it a Completion condition that the Buyer can waive: effective, unconditional consent (or consent with cl 11.3 conditions evidenced as satisfied), backed by a stronger efforts obligation.
- **Reason:** Bluefen is about 30% of FY26 revenue (around AUD 3.6m), and a consent with unmet conditions may not be effective.

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller:** A release "to be provided following Completion" (cl 2 / 7). DL 3 confirms about AUD 3.2m is outstanding, not repaid, and has no discharge.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - a current payout letter;
  - direct repayment from Completion funds;
  - effective security releases at Completion.

  A post-Completion release would need an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval. Neither exists.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject.** Require the payout letter, repayment to Riverlark in the funds flow, and executed releases (including PPSR discharges) delivered at Completion.
- **Reason:** On a debt-free basis, we would otherwise be acquiring a company still encumbered by AUD 3.2m of secured debt, with change-of-control exposure under cl 8.1.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller:** The DD-005 bonuses of AUD 420,000 are "a matter for the Seller" and are not itemised in the funds flow. DL 5 does not address payroll tax, super or on-costs.
- **Buyer wants:** The AUD 420k plus any triggered on-costs either shown as a specific funds-flow line item (Debt-like, deducted from price) or funded by the Seller. The funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Itemise the bonuses plus on-costs in the funds flow, and add a Seller indemnity** for any shortfall or related tax or superannuation.
- **Reason:** These are Company obligations triggered by Completion. "A matter for the Seller" has no mechanism behind it, so the cost would land on the Company we are buying.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** The cl 11.1 indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and described as "adequate."
- **Buyer wants:** A broader indemnity covering all loss from any failure of SOW3 Project Materials to vest, third-party claims, and the cost of re-development or replacement. It should keep the SOW3 cure (payment of all SOW3 fees plus a confirmatory assignment).
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the narrow scope; broaden it, preserve the cure, and require a confirmatory assignment** (pre-Completion if possible).
- **Reason:** Under DD-004 cl 7.3, the IP transfers only on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee, and there is no evidence of payment or assignment.
- **On the AUD 180,000:** The DD-010 figure is not independently verified either way. Do not treat it as confirmed unpaid or as the true exposure.

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006)
- **Seller:** A "preliminary operational matter… not expected to be material" (cl 4.6 / Sch 6).
- **Buyer wants:**
  - log preservation;
  - a proper investigation;
  - regular updates to the Buyer;
  - Buyer input on any notification decision.

  Neither side should characterise the incident as a confirmed breach, as harmful, or as requiring notification. Nor should either side dismiss it.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the "not material" characterisation.** Add pre-Completion covenants (preserve logs, investigate, provide updates, consult on notifications) and a specific indemnity for loss arising from the incident.
- **Reason:** About 1,240 records may be affected. Access, scope and notification duty are all unresolved, so neither a materiality conclusion nor a numeric demand is supported.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller:** The three renewals (3 x AUD 110k = AUD 330k) are ordinary-course costs.
- **Buyer wants:** An assessment, without automatically classifying them as Debt or deducting them from the price. The disclosure does not say whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- **Recommendation:** **Do not accept "ordinary course" as settled. Request information** on terms, timing, termination rights, accrual and the related-party nature (DD-008 / DD-011), then decide on treatment.
- **Reason:** The facts are incomplete, so neither the Seller's characterisation nor a price deduction is justified yet.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** Limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance clauses apply to all Claims "unless expressly stated otherwise." Tax and IP are folded into the general regime.
- **Buyer wants:** Title, Tax, IP, payment obligations and covenants kept as separate categories, with no hidden override by the general regime.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject.** Scope cl 12 limitations expressly to General Warranty Claims. Add an express statement that they do not apply to Fundamental, Tax, IP-indemnity, specific-indemnity, payment or covenant claims.
- **Reason:** The "all Claims" drafting is the mechanism that collapses every protection into a 20% / 18-month regime.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title is evidenced by the DD-012 share register. DL 10 concedes the Buyer has not completed its own verification.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority. DD-012 is an internal source supplied by the Seller, not independent proof.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject reliance on DD-012 alone.** Require:
  - an ASIC company extract consistent with the register;
  - share certificates;
  - PPSR searches against the Company and the Seller;
  - Seller board authority;
  - confirmation of no options or rights;
  - executed share transfers;
  - all of the above backed by an uncapped Fundamental title warranty.
- **Reason:** An internal register cannot prove that title is clear of encumbrances or that the Seller has authority to sell. This matters especially given the Riverlark security.

### SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** Tax and IP warranties are "settled under the general regime."
- **Buyer wants:** Tax and IP terms treated as OPEN. Do not assume any resolution, and do not assume unlimited liability either.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the claim that they are settled. Record Tax and IP as open items** for separate negotiation, outside the general cap, basket and time limit.
- **Reason:** No agreement has been reached, and folding them into the general regime would pre-empt that negotiation.

---

## Other points noted (outside the 16 issues)
- **Office lease (DL 7) and Mossvale (DL 9):** The Seller says only notification or assignment restrictions apply, with no consent needed on a share sale. Please have counsel verify this against DD-007 and DD-009 rather than relying on the Seller's description.
- **DL 1.4 (no admission of liability):** Acceptable in principle. However, it should not dilute the specific disclosures or our indemnities.

**Overall:** All 16 positions sit below or outside our playbook, and several (N-005, N-008, N-009, N-010, N-014) are structural. I recommend a full mark-up on playbook terms. No fallbacks should be offered unless Amelia Frost gives written authority identifying this draft.

- **Seller:** A "preliminary operational matter… not expected to be material" (cl 4.6 / Sch 6).
- **Buyer wants:**
  - log preservation;
  - a proper investigation;
  - regular updates to the Buyer;
  - Buyer input on any notification decision.

  Neither side should characterise the incident as a confirmed breach, as harmful, or as requiring notification. Nor should either side dismiss it.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the "not material" characterisation.** Add pre-Completion covenants (preserve logs, investigate, provide updates, consult on notifications) and a specific indemnity for loss arising from the incident.
- **Reason:** About 1,240 records may be affected. Access, scope and notification duty are all unresolved, so neither a materiality conclusion nor a numeric demand is supported.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller:** The three renewals (3 x AUD 110k = AUD 330k) are ordinary-course costs.
- **Buyer wants:** An assessment, without automatically classifying them as Debt or deducting them from the price. The disclosure does not say whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- **Recommendation:** **Do not accept "ordinary course" as settled. Request information** on terms, timing, termination rights, accrual and the related-party nature (DD-008 / DD-011), then decide on treatment.
- **Reason:** The facts are incomplete, so neither the Seller's characterisation nor a price deduction is justified yet.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** Limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance clauses apply to all Claims "unless expressly stated otherwise." Tax and IP are folded into the general regime.
- **Buyer wants:** Title, Tax, IP, payment obligations and covenants kept as separate categories, with no hidden override by the general regime.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject.** Scope cl 12 limitations expressly to General Warranty Claims. Add an express statement that they do not apply to Fundamental, Tax, IP-indemnity, specific-indemnity, payment or covenant claims.
- **Reason:** The "all Claims" drafting is the mechanism that collapses every protection into a 20% / 18-month regime.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title is evidenced by the DD-012 share register. DL 10 concedes the Buyer has not completed its own verification.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority. DD-012 is an internal source supplied by the Seller, not independent proof.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject reliance on DD-012 alone.** Require:
  - an ASIC company extract consistent with the register;
  - share certificates;
  - PPSR searches against the Company and the Seller;
  - Seller board authority;
  - confirmation of no options or rights;
  - executed share transfers;
  - all of the above backed by an uncapped Fundamental title warranty.
- **Reason:** An internal register cannot prove that title is clear of encumbrances or that the Seller has authority to sell. This matters especially given the Riverlark security.

### SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** Tax and IP warranties are "settled under the general regime."
- **Buyer wants:** Tax and IP terms treated as OPEN. Do not assume any resolution, and do not assume unlimited liability either.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the claim that they are settled. Record Tax and IP as open items** for separate negotiation, outside the general cap, basket and time limit.
- **Reason:** No agreement has been reached, and folding them into the general regime would pre-empt that negotiation.
